lines.hire: Keep the mud dry under my boots and the stew warm, and I'll hold your flank until the iron bends.
lines.refuse: No peat-bogs left to drain here, and I don't bleed for promises that won't buy salt.
lines.price: One hundred five crowns upfront, twenty-two every seventh bell—plus two coppers if you ask me to ford chest-deep water.
lines.loyal25: You're quick to spend another man's ribs while keeping your own cloak clean. Watch how long that lasts.
lines.loyal50: The coin arrives on time and the rations aren't rotten. That puts you a cut above the Thornwick bailiff.
lines.loyal75: I've stood behind worse captains in deeper ditches. Point the ash-shaft where you want the line to hold.
lines.loyal100: My bridge-tithe is cleared and my boots are dry. When the horn blows, nobody gets past my pike to reach you.
lines.leave: My tally's settled and my kettle-helm's dented enough. Keep your silver; I'm walking back to the bog.

lines.hire: Point me toward the upwind brush and keep the heavy-armored clankers twenty paces behind my bowstring.
lines.refuse: Too many loud boots and too little cover in your outfit. Find someone else to scare your quarry away.
lines.price: One hundred fifteen crowns to string my yew, and twenty-four a week for goose-feathers, wax, and quiet.
lines.loyal25: Keep shouting orders like a magistrate's hound and you'll catch a stray bodkin in your own saddlebag.
lines.loyal50: You let me pick my own perches and don't ask where the extra rings came from. Fair enough.
lines.loyal75: We move clean together, captain. Say the word and the lead scout drops before his heel touches moss.
lines.loyal100: This branded ear aches less when I'm hunting beside someone who respects silence. You've got my last arrow.
lines.leave: The wind's shifted and the pickings here have gone sour. I'm fading back into the alder brush.

lines.hire: Give me a dry corner out of the wind and two fingers of juniper spirit, and I'll keep your guts tucked inside.
lines.refuse: Look at the rust on your blades—I'm a barber-surgeon, not a miracle worker for walking corpses.
lines.price: One hundred twenty-five crowns for the kit, twenty-six weekly for catgut, mutton-fat salve, and clean linen.
lines.loyal25: My hands shake worse when you bark at me mid-suture. Keep your distance or stitch your own thigh.
lines.loyal50: Not a bad company, all told. Nobody's died of gangrene on my watch yet, and the gin's passable.
lines.loyal75: You actually listen when I say a wound needs boiling wine instead of a forced march. I'll keep you breathing.
lines.loyal100: Oakhaven's guild threw me out for watering laudanum, yet you trusted me with your own skin. I won't let you bleed out.
lines.leave: I'm out of thread, out of spirits, and out of patience for fresh holes in old meat. Find another leech.

lines.hire: Show me the thickest shield-wall they've got and stand clear when I start my backswing.
lines.refuse: Your timber's rotten and your march is aimless. I don't swing a broad-axe for nothing.
lines.price: One hundred thirty crowns down, twenty-seven each week to keep the whetstone wet and my belly full.
lines.loyal25: You treat men like cheap kindling tossed into a wet hearth. Careful the smoke doesn't choke you.
lines.loyal50: Good solid work, steady camps, and plenty of thick skulls to split. No complaints from the woods.
lines.loyal75: You know how to read a line the way a feller reads grain in old oak. Just point where to strike.
lines.loyal100: Raiders burned my camp to ash, yet this company feels like solid pine underfoot. I'll split any gate for you.
lines.leave: My axe-edge is notched and the timber here isn't worth the sweat. I'm heading north to real trees.

lines.hire: Keep the lamp-oil corked and the dry brush behind me, and I'll turn their vanguard into cinders.
lines.refuse: Too damp, too cramped, and you look like the sort who counts every spark. Find a duller caster.
lines.price: One hundred thirty-five crowns upfront, twenty-eight weekly—and don't dock my pay for scorched bedrolls.
lines.loyal25: Keep lecturing me about singed eyebrows and I might forget which direction the wind is blowing.
lines.loyal50: You give me room to cast and don't panic when the air smells like tallow. That's rare.
lines.loyal75: The prior said I lacked discipline, yet you've turned my bad habits into dead enemies. I like your methods.
lines.loyal100: I pawned temple brass to survive, and you gave me a real furnace to feed. Say the word and I'll burn the sky.
lines.leave: The wick's burned down to the grease here. I'm taking my scrolls before someone blames me for the next fire.

lines.hire: Keep the bodies reasonably whole and the ground soft enough for a spade, and we'll make a tidy profit.
lines.refuse: You leave too many ashes and broken bones behind—poor return on labor for an honest sexton.
lines.price: One hundred forty crowns retainer, twenty-eight a week, plus burial rights on whatever falls unclaimed.
lines.loyal25: I've already measured your shoulders with my knotted cord, captain. Don't make me dig early.
lines.loyal50: Prompt wages and fresh turf every third march. My ledger balances nicely under your command.
lines.loyal75: You understand that the dead owe a debt to the living who kept them fed. A rare pragmatism.
lines.loyal100: Twelve winters in Thornwick's flooded yard taught me loyalty belongs to those who pay the shovel-fee. I'm yours to the grave.
lines.leave: The soil here is too rocky and your casualties are too messy. I'm closing the parish roll.

lines.hire: Fill my canteen with sweet water and give me twenty paces of open salt-flat—I'll crack their helmets open.
lines.refuse: Dry marches with no silver at the end? I already lost my brine-pans to bandits; I won't lose my hide to you.
lines.price: Two hundred ninety crowns for the sling and lead shot, fifty-five weekly for water-skin and salt-tax.
lines.loyal25: Keep marching us into the glare without shade and I'll test my sling-stones on your canteens.
lines.loyal50: You know how to ration water in the flats and pick targets worth the lead. We're square.
lines.loyal75: My teeth are stained red from alkali root, but my aim's never been steadier than under your banner.
lines.loyal100: You gave a stripped drover back his pride and a pouch of good lead. No viper in Redmarsh touches you.
lines.leave: My tongue's like dried leather and the silver's too thin for this heat. Find another slinger.

lines.hire: Point out the thickest wall, carapace, or gatehouse, and keep everyone back when my pick finds the seam.
lines.refuse: If you expect me to bunk inside stone barracks, keep your coin. I've had enough ceilings over my head.
lines.price: Three hundred ten crowns down, fifty-eight each week—paid in silver, never iron script.
lines.loyal25: Order me into another cramped vault without timber props and I'll swing this pick at the door-hinges instead.
lines.loyal50: Open sky at night and solid stone to crack by day. You run a fair shift, captain.
lines.loyal75: Three years in Gorrathul's chains taught me who breaks first. You're forged harder than most.
lines.loyal100: I sleep under the stars without nightmares for the first time since the quarry. Every wall before you is dust.
lines.leave: My lungs are full of grit and your marches smell too much like prison tunnels. I'm done digging.

lines.hire: Let me run loose ahead of the column and read the sand-drifts—your boots won't touch a single ambush.
lines.refuse: You march like a parade of tin kettles. Every dune-lurker in Redmarsh hears you three leagues off.
lines.price: Three hundred twenty-five crowns to take the trail, sixty weekly for dried meat, oil, and silence.
lines.loyal25: Force me back into your tight little ranks again and I'll vanish before the next watch-fire burns down.
lines.loyal50: You trust my eyes on the dunes and pay without haggling over every arrow. Good enough.
lines.loyal75: Few captains understand that a scout's worth lies twenty paces outside their sight. You've earned my trust.
lines.loyal100: The magistrates cheated me out of bounties, yet you've never shorted a copper. I'll track your enemies to the bone.
lines.leave: The wind's erasing the tracks and my quiver's down to lizard jerky. I'm taking the high ridge alone.

lines.hire: Keep steel away from my robes and I'll keep your armored men from cooking inside their own breastplates.
lines.refuse: You waste water like a drunken factor and pray to nothing. My wards won't hold over ungrateful dust.
lines.price: Three hundred thirty crowns for the blessing, sixty-two weekly for clean flasks and salt-incense.
lines.loyal25: Mock my puddle-prayers one more time and see how fast your throat cracks in the midday glare.
lines.loyal50: You respect the cistern-wards and keep the frontline steady while I chant. Peace be upon your canteens.
lines.loyal75: The hermitage cast me out for watering melons, yet here my rain actually saves lives. You've given me purpose.
lines.loyal100: Every well we cross feels blessed under your command. So long as breath remains in me, you will never thirst.
lines.leave: The flasks are dry and my prayers bounce off your iron skulls. May the desert teach you humility.

lines.hire: Provide the targets and keep the dust off my inkpot; I shall serve the Third Dynasty's overdue writs.
lines.refuse: Your campaign lacks proper documentation and your casualties leave messy ledgers. I decline.
lines.price: Three hundred forty-five crowns filing fee, sixty-four weekly for papyrus strips, gum-ink, and astral seal.
lines.loyal25: My left hand may be stiff as leather, captain, but my right still writes arrears beside your name.
lines.loyal50: Punctual disbursements and orderly engagements. You conduct war with admirable clerical rigor.
lines.loyal75: Zahra's expedition left me with a cursed hand; your company gave that hex gainful employment.
lines.loyal100: Every notch on my belt-papyrus honors our shared enterprise. When your final hour comes, I shall balance your book cleanly.
lines.leave: The ink has thickened in the heat and your accounts have grown erratic. I hereby close this file.

lines.hire: Put silver in my palm before the horn sounds, and nothing living crosses the rim of my kite shield.
lines.refuse: I watched twelve good men butchered because a merchant counted coppers. You smell of the same thrift.
lines.price: Three hundred sixty crowns upfront, sixty-six every seventh day—counted in daylight, never by torchlight.
lines.loyal25: Short my quiver-allowance once more and I'll step aside the next time cavalry charges your banner.
lines.loyal50: You buy enough arrows and pay before the blood dries. That's all I ask of any commander.
lines.loyal75: I sleep with my shield strapped to my arm, yet beside your campfires I actually close both eyes.
lines.loyal100: Bram's lot died for a miser's purse, but you spend silver to keep men alive. My shield stays yours till it splits.
lines.leave: My shield-rim's chewed to splinters and the margin's getting too thin. Count me out before the next pass.

lines.hire: Point me at the tightest breach or gangplank and keep rum out of the surgeons' tent till the deck is clear.
lines.refuse: Too much open running and not enough shield-to-shield grit. Find a landlubber for your skirmishes.
lines.price: Seven hundred twenty crowns to sign articles, one hundred twenty weekly—paid in dry silver.
lines.loyal25: Keep flinching from a proper boarding-crush and I'll toss my cutlass overboard and swim home.
lines.loyal50: Steady rations, dry powder, and officers who don't hide behind the rigging. Aye, I'll stay aboard.
lines.loyal75: Lost two toes on the winter blockade, yet you've made mud trenches feel like a well-run cutter.
lines.loyal100: I've sailed under admirals who couldn't hold a candle to your nerve. Say the word and we board hell itself.
lines.leave: The bilge is rising and the wind's foul. I'm taking my sea-chest ashore before this tub founders.

lines.hire: Give me three dry heartbeats to crank the windlass, and I'll punch steel straight through their breastplates.
lines.refuse: No parapet, no cover, and too many fools standing in my firing lane. Find another arbalestier.
lines.price: Seven hundred sixty crowns down, one hundred twenty-five weekly for steel prods, grease, and hemp cord.
lines.loyal25: Rush my reload again and the next bolt might slip off the nut while you're standing in front.
lines.loyal50: You hold the line long enough for my windlass to click. That's all a heavy prod needs.
lines.loyal75: Ten years on the customs tower never gave me cleaner targets than your flanking maneuvers do.
lines.loyal100: Every officer-notch on my stock was earned under your eye. Name the heaviest plate on the field; it's dead.
lines.leave: My windlass teeth are worn smooth and my shoulders ache in the salt damp. I'm unspanning for good.

lines.hire: Keep iron pikes clear of my sleeves when the clouds gather, and I'll turn their wet armor into copper wire.
lines.refuse: Dry air and cautious tactics—neither conducts lightning worth a damn. Look elsewhere.
lines.price: Eight hundred crowns retainer, one hundred thirty-two weekly—plus extra if I ruin another pair of rubber soles.
lines.loyal25: Stand too close with that steel halberd when I'm charged and we'll both smell like fried harbor gull.
lines.loyal50: You keep the infantry grounded and give me clear sightlines when the squall hits. Fair bargain.
lines.loyal75: Oakhaven's weather-guild called me reckless; you call it artillery. I like working for a realist.
lines.loyal100: The storm answers faster when you call the strike, captain. Together we'll make the Iron Coast glow.
lines.leave: The static's gone dead and your caution grounds every spark I raise. I'm drifting back to the lighthouse.

lines.hire: Try to take your wounds cleanly across the muscle; ragged tears waste half my vinegar and all my patience.
lines.refuse: Look at the collarbone structure on your vanguard—brittle as chalk. I won't waste good sutures here.
lines.price: Seven hundred ninety crowns for the saw-case, one hundred thirty weekly for spirit, catgut, and silence.
lines.loyal25: Keep throwing men into meat-grinders without shield support and I'll start charging by the limb.
lines.loyal50: Decent survival odds, clean camp-ditches, and nobody rummaging through my specimen jars. Acceptable.
lines.loyal75: Chief Healer Sera hated my pragmatism, yet you appreciate that a living cripple beats a pretty corpse.
lines.loyal100: I've seen every bone in your body through my fingers, captain, and none of them belong in a ditch. I'll keep you whole.
lines.leave: My forceps are dulled and your survival odds just dipped below my fee. Find another sawbones.

lines.hire: The tide remembers every oath sworn over salt water; let me ring the bell and collect what your foes owe.
lines.refuse: Your cause carries no weight beneath the waves, and the drowned will not stir for shallow pockets.
lines.price: Eight hundred twenty crowns in stamped silver, one hundred thirty-six weekly—and keep shellfish off my plate.
lines.loyal25: Break another promise made at low tide and my brass bell will ring for your own shroud.
lines.loyal50: You honor your contracts and keep the hexers pinned while I pronounce judgment. The sea approves.
lines.loyal75: Few living commanders command the respect of those beneath the surf. Your word carries cold authority.
lines.loyal100: When my brass bell tolls beside you, even the drowned stand at attention. My ledger and my life are yours.
lines.leave: The tide turns outward and the drowned grow quiet in your wake. I return to the wreck-shrine.

lines.hire: Silver weighs the same under any banner—just keep yours upright and don't try paying me in clipped tin.
lines.refuse: Your purse sounds light and your odds look worse. I've walked off richer losing sides than this.
lines.price: Eight hundred fifty crowns down, one hundred forty every seventh day—weighed on my own scale.
lines.loyal25: If my teeth find lead beneath your silver plating, I'll switch sides before your horn finishes blowing.
lines.loyal50: Honest weight, solid brigandine salvage, and no speeches about honor. Best contract I've signed this year.
lines.loyal75: I walked away from Sundered Ranks without looking back, yet here I actually care whether the flank holds.
lines.loyal100: Keep your gold—I bite your coins out of habit now, not suspicion. No warlord alive could buy me off your line.
lines.leave: The margin's gone sour and my brigandine's taking more dents than silver. Contract terminated.

lines.hire: Keep my boots oiled against the sulfur crust and I'll hook their champions right out of the ash.
lines.refuse: You haven't breathed enough caldera grit to know what waits behind the vents. Come back when you're hardened.
lines.price: One thousand five hundred twenty crowns upfront, two hundred forty weekly—paid before we cross the slag.
lines.loyal25: Send me into demon-plate without flank support again and I'll leave my halberd stuck in your standard.
lines.loyal50: You know how to anchor a shield-line against heat and heavy steel. Ironcamp would respect that.
lines.loyal75: My eyebrows never grew back after Greystone, yet standing beside you feels like holding the wall all over again.
lines.loyal100: Tell Rowan I found a commander worth bleeding in the sulfur for. Nothing breaks through while I hold the haft.
lines.leave: My pumice is worn flat and my boots are cracking in the vents. I'm marching back to Ironcamp.

lines.hire: Mark the priority target and stay out of my sightline—heat shimmer bends arrows, never my aim.
lines.refuse: You move too loudly across open crags and leave your flanks exposed to updrafts. Find a noisier bow.
lines.price: One thousand five hundred eighty crowns to string, two hundred fifty weekly for redglass splinters and oil.
lines.loyal25: Keep blocking my view with erratic charges and I'll pack my smoked-quartz goggles tonight.
lines.loyal50: Clean target calls, steady perches, and no complaints about the ash in my rations. Good work.
lines.loyal75: Hunting redglass drakes taught me patience, but your tactical timing makes every shot effortless.
lines.loyal100: Even in the darkest vaults I see the kill clearly beside you. Name any champion; they're already dead.
lines.leave: The thermal winds have turned erratic and my splinters are running low. I'm taking the high crag.

lines.hire: Everything in this caldera burns white-hot; keep steel off my robes and I'll bring the glacier.
lines.refuse: You charge into fissure-vents without wards or sense. I won't waste good frost on cinders.
lines.price: One thousand six hundred fifty crowns down, two hundred sixty weekly—plus oiled felt for my ice-core.
lines.loyal25: One more reckless rush into magma-vents and you can quench your own armor with sweat.
lines.loyal50: You time your infantry strikes right as my frost locks their joints. Proper foundry discipline.
lines.loyal75: At Ironcamp we quenched blades; with you we shatter whole vanguard lines. My runes run cold and true.
lines.loyal100: My glacier-core hasn't melted an ounce since joining your banner. Together we'll freeze the Ember Court solid.
lines.leave: The heat's cracking my wards and my glacier-chunk is down to a pebble. I'm returning to the foundries.

lines.hire: My debt is written in hot ash across my eyes; let me stand between your company and the flame.
lines.refuse: Your hands are heavy with unrepented greed. I will not walk into hellfire for another tax-collector.
lines.price: One thousand six hundred crowns to fund the orphans' alms, two hundred fifty-five weekly—not a copper for myself.
lines.loyal25: Count my heartbeat near the magma—it slows whenever you waste lives for vanity.
lines.loyal50: You walk into the dark with steady purpose rather than pride. My penance finds meaning here.
lines.loyal75: Once I blinded myself for the sins of the Ember Court; now your leadership shows me a cleaner path.
lines.loyal100: Every scar on my chest sings when I hold the standard beside you. Let the cinders fall; I will not yield.
lines.leave: My debt here is paid in blood and ash, and our paths diverge before the final gate. Walk in the quiet dark.

lines.hire: The First Watch never received their discharge papers; grant me leave to summon them from the ash.
lines.refuse: You treat sworn oaths as disposable parchment. The Threshold catacombs will not lend you their dead.
lines.price: One thousand seven hundred twenty crowns archival tithe, two hundred seventy weekly for brass wax and vellum.
lines.loyal25: Break faith with your living soldiers and see how swiftly the First Watch turns its pikes inward.
lines.loyal50: You honor every pact down to the last copper. The ancient watchmen respect such discipline.
lines.loyal75: Three decades beneath the obsidian floor taught me to recognize true authority. Your seal carries weight.
lines.loyal100: When I polish my brass weights beside your tent, the ancestors themselves stand ready to serve their term.
lines.leave: The ledger is sealed and the First Watch has fulfilled its writ. I return to the Threshold.

lines.hire: Keep open flames three paces off my belt and I'll turn their iron golems into smoking gravel.
lines.refuse: Too many careless torches and sloppy marches. I've lost three fingers already; I won't lose the rest for you.
lines.price: One thousand seven hundred eighty crowns for prism-powder, two hundred eighty weekly—paid before every fuse is lit.
lines.loyal25: Wave another torch near my satchel and I'll let the next siege-golem walk straight over your tent.
lines.loyal50: You keep the torches back and give me clean angles on the portcullis. That's all a sapper asks.
lines.loyal75: Seven fingers are plenty when a commander knows exactly where to place a charge. You've got a good eye.
lines.loyal100: No sulfur leak escapes my nose and no fortress gate survives our partnership. Just say when to light the fuse.
lines.leave: My powder's damp and my remaining fingers are twitching. I'm packing my charges before something blows.
